clue.text: EU makes speeches about the end of irregular vegetables

parts.note: Brussels is the seat of the European Union, so the city stands for it

indicators.note: about means around, so the speechmaking wraps round the next piece

parts.note: to spout is to hold forth, speechifying at length

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, taken from irregular here

parts.note: the word whose final letter is used

explanation.surface: A dig at European bureaucrats whose oddly shaped vegetables are the subject of pompous speeches.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the old tabloid stories about EU rules on misshapen produce; here 'EU' is simply the city that houses it.
explanation.definitionFit: These small green brassicas, named after the Belgian capital, are a familiar winter vegetable.

clue.text: Sat badly in toboggan that hurt

indicators.note: in tells us the cry of pain sits inside the sledge

parts.note: a sled is a small sledge, like a toboggan
OUCH is the exclamation you make when something hurts

explanation.surface: Someone sat awkwardly on a toboggan and ended up in pain.
explanation.definitionFit: To slouch is to sit with drooping shoulders and poor posture, so the past tense means sat badly.

clue.text: Welshman taken in by shady landlord

indicators.note: the name is taken in, or contained, by the run of letters across these two words

parts.note: the words that conceal the name

explanation.surface: A man from Wales is conned by a dodgy landlord.
explanation.walkthrough: Dylan Thomas is the most famous bearer of this Welsh first name.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional Welsh male name, borne most famously by the poet Dylan Thomas.

clue.text: Leader of orchestra will acknowledge applause

definitions.meaning: first meaning, playfully: an orchestra's leader is its principal violinist, who will pick up a violin bow
second meaning: bend at the waist in thanks to the audience

explanation.surface: At the end of a concert the first violinist stands to receive the clapping.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase can be read as the violinist literally picking up a bow for the instrument, as well as bowing to the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Performers bend forward in thanks at a curtain call, the stock gesture for accepting a round of clapping.

clue.text: Individual finally asleep with horrible snore

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word asleep

parts.note: the word whose final letter is used

indicators.note: horrible suggests the letters of snore are mangled into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone finally nods off, only to produce a dreadful snore.
explanation.definitionFit: A single human being is an individual, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Roughly shaking awake for drinking session

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about or roughly
arousing someone is waking them up, perhaps by shaking

explanation.surface: Someone is roughly shaken awake after a heavy night out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roughly shaking' looks like an anagram signal, but 'Roughly' is circa and 'shaking awake' is a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Carousing is lively, noisy drinking in company, used here as a noun for such a bout.

clue.text: Ring for seats here in the theatre

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a round shape or loop
second meaning: the dress ... or upper ..., a tier of theatre seating

explanation.walkthrough: Theatre seating is divided into stalls, circle and balcony, so the curved tier is named by the same word as a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a round shape and also the curved upper tier of seats in a playhouse.

clue.text: In this part of the country athletic kit's red, surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly hints that the letters of the kit description turn out in an unexpected order

parts.note: anagram fodder, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A local sports team in some region turns out in red strip, which is a surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lake District is a mountainous national park in Cumbria, north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lake District is a region of England, so it is a part of the country.

clue.text: If you start this event, you will never reach the end

definitions.text: If you start this event, you will never reach the end

parts.note: in a team race the first runner starts it off

parts.words: you will never reach the end
parts.note: the opening runner hands on the baton, so another teammate crosses the finish line

explanation.surface: A gloomy warning that some task can never be completed once begun.
explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a counsel of despair, but it simply describes the first leg of a team race.
explanation.definitionFit: In this team event each runner covers one leg and passes a baton, so the starter never runs to the finish.

clue.text: US sect quiet beside a motorway

indicators.note: beside places the quiet sign next to the motorway

parts.note: taken as written
the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway; the digit 1 is read as the letter I
SH is the hushing sound asking for quiet

explanation.surface: A religious group keeps quiet, living beside a motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amish are a Christian community in the United States known for shunning modern technology.

clue.text: Cooked meat eaten in tube

parts.note: suggests a snack eaten on the London Underground
really describes minced meat packed into a tubular skin

explanation.surface: Someone eats a cooked meat snack on the London Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is London's Underground railway, which the surface evokes; the real tube is the casing.
explanation.definitionFit: This is seasoned minced meat stuffed into a tubular casing, then cooked.

clue.text: Long-suffering cat treated with oils

indicators.note: treated suggests the letters are processed and rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder
anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A patient pet cat is given an application of oils.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoical person endures hardship without complaint, much like someone patiently long-suffering.

clue.text: Bouncer in city house

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London

explanation.surface: A doorman working at a house in town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bouncer' suggests a nightclub doorman, but here it is a sound that rebounds off a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo is a sound reflected back from a wall or cliff, so it literally bounces.

clue.text: Take on bets, after arranging a cut

indicators.note: arranging the letters puts them into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A bookmaker accepts wagers and then organises some sort of cut.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a cut of beef containing a T-shaped bone, with sirloin on one side and fillet on the other.

clue.text: Prairie fare is nothing spicy

definitions.meaning: first meaning, whimsically: food from the plains, such as a prairie is

explanation.walkthrough: A prairie is a plain, so its food can playfully be called by the same phrase as unspiced cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: Simple unseasoned cooking is the usual sense; the first reading jokes that a plain is a prairie.

clue.text: This is how daughter prepared cabbage: why does it all go wrong?

definitions.text: why does it all go wrong?
definitions.note: a noun phrase answering the question: the reason things always go wrong

parts.note: so can mean in this way, as in 'do it so'
slaw is coleslaw, a salad of shredded raw cabbage

explanation.surface: A daughter's cabbage dish has gone badly, prompting a despairing question.
explanation.walkthrough: Sod's Law is the British name for the rule that whatever can go wrong will, like Murphy's Law.
explanation.definitionFit: This mock principle says that whatever can misfire will, so it answers the exasperated question.

clue.text: Country is fine away from the coast

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
inland means in the interior, far from the sea

explanation.surface: A country where the weather is lovely once you leave the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites FINE + LAND, but only F comes from 'fine'.
explanation.definitionFit: Finland is a Nordic nation bordering Sweden, Norway and Russia.

clue.text: The basis of bread is hard to grow profusely

parts.note: flour is the main ingredient of bread
taken as written

explanation.surface: A baker's observation that getting dough to rise well is tricky.
explanation.definitionFit: To flourish is to thrive and grow vigorously, as plants do in good conditions.

clue.text: Each sigh movingly suggests one is more valuable than a king

definitions.text: suggests one is more valuable than a king
definitions.note: read as a description of what the phrase itself conveys

indicators.note: movingly hints that the letters move about into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Emotional sighs hint that someone values a single thing above royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: In card games played aces high, the ace (a one) outranks the king.
explanation.definitionFit: When aces are ranked highest, the card bearing one pip beats the king in card games.

clue.text: Bear walking along and not returning

parts.note: padding is walking softly and steadily

indicators.note: returning means the word not is read backwards

parts.note: the word to be read backwards

explanation.surface: A bear is out walking and will not be coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: Paddington is the marmalade-loving bear of Michael Bond's children's books, named after the London station.
explanation.definitionFit: Paddington is a famous fictional bear from Peru, found at a London railway station.

clue.text: Very attractive male ready to dance

indicators.note: to dance suggests the letters are jigged around into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A handsome man is all set to hit the dance floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreamy is informal for gorgeous, someone so appealing they seem out of a fantasy.

clue.text: Making fun of man about to be burned?

definitions.text: Making fun of man about to be burned?

parts.note: to guy someone is to ridicule them
hints at the guy, the effigy of Guy Fawkes burned on Bonfire Night

explanation.surface: Mocking someone who is about to be burnt at the stake.
explanation.walkthrough: On Bonfire Night, 5 November, Britons burn an effigy called a guy, recalling the Gunpowder Plot's Guy Fawkes.
explanation.definitionFit: Guying means mocking, a verb derived from the ridiculous effigies paraded before burning.

clue.text: Some coming back assemble in dining hall

indicators.note: coming back means the chosen letters are read backwards
some means only part of the next word is used

parts.note: the word holding the letters

explanation.surface: A few people return to gather in the canteen.
explanation.definitionFit: A mess is the room where members of the armed forces eat together.

clue.text: Said to require massage

indicators.note: said means the word is spoken, so we want something that sounds the same

parts.note: to need something is to require it

explanation.surface: Someone is told they need a rubdown.
explanation.definitionFit: To knead is to work and press with the hands, as a masseur does to muscles or a baker to dough.

clue.text: Miss out on being in a plane?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: skip a place by passing over it
second meaning, literal: travel over somewhere by air

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether missing an experience means being stuck on a flight.
explanation.walkthrough: To fly over a place is to pass it by from the air without stopping.
explanation.definitionFit: To overfly a place is to travel above it by aircraft, thereby passing it by.

clue.text: Farmer fled, caught by some woman

parts.note: ran away is to have fled
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
her refers to an unspecified woman

explanation.surface: A farmer bolted but was seized by a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught by' looks like a containment signal, but C is just caught, followed by HER.
explanation.definitionFit: A rancher runs a large livestock farm, especially in North America.

clue.text: Speed of work was satisfying, just about

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so this signals reading the pieces backwards

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work
met as in met the requirements, satisfied them

explanation.surface: The pace of a job was almost satisfactory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just about' looks like 'nearly' but signals the pieces are turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempo is the pace of a piece of music, hence its rate or velocity.

clue.text: Wistful, losing cat in a crash

indicators.note: a crash smashes things up, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone is sad after their cat is lost in an accident.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostalgic means longingly remembering the past, a melancholy yearning close to wistful.
